name: Darbepoetin alfa
route_note: IV or SC injection once weekly to once every 2–4 weeks

discovery.by: Amgen scientists (Steve Elliott, Joan Egrie and colleagues)
discovery.note: Engineered EPO with two extra N-linked glycosylation sites; higher sialic acid content slows clearance about threefold.

tagline: Hyperglycosylated EPO analogue allowing less frequent dosing than epoetin
summary: Darbepoetin alfa is an erythropoietin analogue with five N-linked carbohydrate chains instead of three, giving it a roughly threefold longer half-life than epoetin alfa. It treats anaemia of chronic kidney disease and chemotherapy-induced anaemia with weekly or less frequent injections. It carries the class boxed warning for erythropoiesis-stimulating agents.
mechanism: Darbepoetin alfa binds and activates the erythropoietin receptor on erythroid progenitors in the same way as endogenous EPO, stimulating red cell production through JAK2–STAT5 signalling.

Five amino-acid substitutions create two additional N-glycosylation sites. The extra sialic-acid-rich carbohydrate lowers receptor affinity but greatly reduces clearance, so the net in vivo potency per dose and duration are higher.
uses: Anaemia due to chronic kidney disease
Anaemia due to myelosuppressive chemotherapy in non-myeloid malignancies

history.title: Design
history.detail: Amgen researchers begin adding glycosylation sites to EPO to extend its half-life.

history.title: Approvals
history.detail: FDA and EU approve Aranesp for anaemia of chronic renal failure.

history.title: Chemotherapy anaemia
history.detail: FDA extends approval to chemotherapy-induced anaemia.

history.title: Boxed warning
history.detail: Class boxed warning on mortality, cardiovascular events and tumour progression added for all ESAs.

history.title: TREAT
history.detail: In diabetic CKD patients not on dialysis, targeting haemoglobin 13 g/dL doubled stroke risk without reducing cardiovascular or renal events.

history.title: Dosing revised
history.detail: FDA labels drop target ranges and advise individualised dosing to the lowest dose avoiding transfusion.

pk.half_life: about 21 hours IV and about 49 hours SC in CKD

safety.boxed_warning: ESAs increase the risk of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, venous thromboembolism, vascular access thrombosis and tumour progression or recurrence; use the lowest dose sufficient to avoid transfusion.

facts: Its name derives from 'darbe' plus 'poetin', and in Japan it is marketed by Kyowa Kirin as Nesp.
